plots.title: Fusion Weight Alpha (α) vs. Retrieval Quality
plots.purpose: Evaluate sensitivity of ranking metrics across the full alpha spectrum from pure semantic (0.0) to pure lexical (1.0).
plots.description: Line plot showing P@1, MRR, and NDCG@5 as lexical weight alpha varies from 0.0 to 1.0 in 0.1 increments on the validation set.
plots.dataset: Amoeba Multi-Language Retrieval Benchmark (Validation Suite, N=10 queries)
plots.methodology: Min-max normalized score fusion H = alpha * L_norm + (1 - alpha) * S_norm across 11 discrete weight steps.
plots.notes: Quality remains stable at P@1: 1.00 for alpha in [0.0, 0.8], dropping to 0.90 at alpha = 1.0 (pure lexical) due to the conceptual query miss.

plots.title: Retrieval & Ranking Quality by Method
plots.purpose: Compare aggregate ranking performance across Baseline Lexical, BM25, CodeAware, Semantic, and Hybrid pipelines.
plots.description: Grouped bar chart displaying P@1, MRR, and NDCG@5 across the 5 primary retrieval architectures evaluated on the validation suite.
plots.methodology: Standard evaluation against ground-truth graded relevance judgments on the multi-language test corpus.
plots.notes: Hybrid retrieval matches semantic retrieval at P@1: 1.00 and MRR: 1.00 while preserving strong syntactic token discrimination.

plots.title: Retrieval Quality (P@1) by Query Category
plots.purpose: Analyze category-level tradeoffs between CodeAware lexical, Semantic, and Hybrid retrieval.
plots.description: Horizontal bar chart comparing P@1 across 10 query categories (1 query per category, N=10 total).
plots.methodology: Evaluates P@1 for each query category under identical test conditions.
plots.notes: Hybrid retrieval preserves 1.00 precision across all 9 lexical categories while resolving the vocabulary mismatch on the conceptual category.

plots.title: Query-Level Outcome Classification
plots.purpose: Quantify query win, loss, and preserved outcomes when fusing lexical and semantic signals.
plots.description: Bar chart categorizing queries into Hybrid Preserved (9/10), Hybrid Improved (1/10), and Hybrid Regressed (0/10).
plots.methodology: Each query is classified based on whether hybrid ranking improves, preserves, or regresses rank-1 precision relative to pure lexical.
plots.notes: No queries regressed under balanced hybrid fusion on this validation suite.

plots.title: Total End-to-End Query Latency by Pipeline
plots.purpose: Compare runtime cost of Lexical Only (0.08ms), Semantic Only (9.69ms), and Full Hybrid (9.80ms).
plots.description: Bar chart comparing CPU query execution latency across the three retrieval pipelines.
plots.methodology: Measured using median CPU timings across repeated executions on x86_64 hardware.
plots.notes: Hybrid query latency is dominated by query text embedding generation (~9.68ms); candidate union and fusion add only ~0.022ms.

plots.title: Candidate Pool Depth vs. Hybrid Ranking Quality
plots.purpose: Examine how semantic candidate depth K (from 3 to 20) affects ranking quality and fusion overhead.
plots.description: Line plot showing NDCG@5 and MRR as candidate pool depth varies.
plots.metric: NDCG@5, MRR vs Candidate Depth K
plots.methodology: Calculates hybrid fusion metrics while capping semantic retriever candidate outputs at discrete K thresholds.
plots.notes: Top-5 semantic candidate depth is sufficient to capture relevant entities on this validation suite.
